sentences.text: Customers now routinely see menus of suggested default options—often well above 20% of what they owe.
sentences.read: Customers now routinely see menus of suggested default options—often well above twenty percent of what they owe.

sentences.text: The amounts have risen from 10% or less in the 1950s to 15% around the year 2000 to 20% or higher today.
sentences.read: The amounts have risen from ten percent or less in the nineteen fifties to fifteen percent around the year two thousand to twenty percent or higher today.

sentences.text: This increase is sometimes called tipflation—the expectation of ever-higher tip amounts.
sentences.read: This increase is sometimes called tipflation—the expectation of ever-higher tip amounts.

sentences.text: Tipping has always been a vital source of income for workers in historically tipped services, like restaurants, where the tipped minimum wage can be as low as US$2.13 an hour.
sentences.read: Tipping has always been a vital source of income for workers in historically tipped services, like restaurants, where the tipped minimum wage can be as low as UStwo point one three dollars an hour.

sentences.text: Tip creep and tipflation are now further supplementing the income of many low-wage service workers.
sentences.read: Tip creep and tipflation are now further supplementing the income of many low-wage service workers.

sentences.text: Notably, tipping primarily benefits some of these workers, such as waiters, but not others, such as cooks and dishwashers.
sentences.read: Notably, tipping primarily benefits some of these workers, such as waiters, but not others, such as cooks and dishwashers.

sentences.text: To ensure that all employees were paid fair wages, some restaurants banned tipping and increased prices, but this movement towards no-tipping services has largely fizzled out.
sentences.read: To ensure that all employees were paid fair wages, some restaurants banned tipping and increased prices, but this movement towards no-tipping services has largely fizzled out.

sentences.text: So to increase employee wages without raising prices, more employers are succumbing to the temptations of tip creep and tipflation.
sentences.read: So to increase employee wages without raising prices, more employers are succumbing to the temptations of tip creep and tipflation.

sentences.text: However, many customers are frustrated because they feel they are being asked for too high a tip too often.
sentences.read: However, many customers are frustrated because they feel they are being asked for too high a tip too often.

sentences.text: And, as our research emphasizes, tipping now seems to be more coercive, less generous, and often completely dissociated from service quality.

sentences.text: When it was established, the National Health Service (NHS) was visionary: offering high-quality, timely care to meet the dominant needs of the population it served.
sentences.read: When it was established, the National Health Service, NHS, was visionary: offering high-quality, timely care to meet the dominant needs of the population it served.

sentences.text: Nearly 75 years on, with the UK facing very different health challenges, it is clear that the model is out of date.
sentences.read: Nearly seventy-five years on, with the UK facing very different health challenges, it is clear that the model is out of date.

sentences.text: From life expectancy to cancer and infant mortality rates, we are lagging behind many of our peers.
sentences.read: From life expectancy to cancer and infant mortality rates, we are lagging behind many of our peers.

sentences.text: With more than 6.8 million on waitlists, healthcare is becoming increasingly inaccessible for those who cannot opt to pay for private treatment; and the cost of providing healthcare is increasingly squeezing our investment in other public services.
sentences.read: With more than six point eight million on waitlists, healthcare is becoming increasingly inaccessible for those who cannot opt to pay for private treatment; and the cost of providing healthcare is increasingly squeezing our investment in other public services.

sentences.text: As demand for healthcare continues to grow, pressures on the workforce—which is already near breaking point—will only become more acute.
sentences.read: As demand for healthcare continues to grow, pressures on the workforce—which is already near breaking point—will only become more acute.

sentences.text: Many of the answers to the crisis in health and care are well rehearsed.
sentences.read: Many of the answers to the crisis in health and care are well rehearsed.

sentences.text: We need to be much better at reducing and diverting demand on health services, rather than simply managing it.
sentences.read: We need to be much better at reducing and diverting demand on health services, rather than simply managing it.

sentences.text: Much more needs to be invested in communities and primary care to reduce our reliance on hospitals.
sentences.read: Much more needs to be invested in communities and primary care to reduce our reliance on hospitals.

sentences.text: And capacity in social care needs to be greater, to support the growing number of people living with long-term conditions.
sentences.read: And capacity in social care needs to be greater, to support the growing number of people living with long-term conditions.

sentences.text: Yet despite two decades of strategies and a number of major health reforms, we have failed to make meaningful progress on any of these aims.
sentences.read: Yet despite two decades of strategies and a number of major health reforms, we have failed to make meaningful progress on any of these aims.

sentences.text: That is why the Reform think tank is launching a new programme of work entitled “Reimagining health”, supported by ten former health ministers.
sentences.read: That is why the Reform think tank is launching a new programme of work entitled “Reimagining health”, supported by ten former health ministers.

sentences.text: Together, we are calling for a much more open and honest conversation about the future of health in the UK, and an “urgent rethink” of the hospital-centric model we retain.
sentences.read: Together, we are calling for a much more open and honest conversation about the future of health in the UK, and an “urgent rethink” of the hospital-centric model we retain.

sentences.text: This must begin with the question of how we maximise the health of the nation, rather than “fix” the NHS.
sentences.read: This must begin with the question of how we maximise the health of the nation, rather than “fix” the NHS.

sentences.text: It is estimated, for example, that healthcare accounts for only about 20% of health outcomes.
sentences.read: It is estimated, for example, that healthcare accounts for only about twenty percent of health outcomes.

sentences.text: Much more important are the places we live, work and socialise—yet there is no clear cross-government strategy for improving these social determinants of health.
sentences.read: Much more important are the places we live, work and socialise—yet there is no clear cross-government strategy for improving these social determinants of health.

sentences.text: Worse, when policies like the national obesity strategy are scrapped, taxpayers are left with the hefty price tag of treating the illnesses, like diabetes, that result.

sentences.text: Reform wants to ask how power and resources should be distributed in our health system.
sentences.read: Reform wants to ask how power and resources should be distributed in our health system.

sentences.text: What health functions should remain at the centre, and what should be given to local leaders, often responsible for services that create health, and with a much better understanding of the needs of their populations?
